extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_short: oath and application data sheet requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for preparing, filing, and correcting oaths/declarations and application data sheets (ADS) in U.S. patent applications, including what must be included, how to identify specifications/priority, when supplemental oaths or ADSs are required, and examiner form paragraph options for defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) labeling and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be labeled 'Application Data Sheet' and should provide specified applicant, inventor, correspondence, application, representative, domestic priority, foreign priority, assignee, and other information fields (inventor given/family names, name suffix, mailing address lines, city, state/province, postal/zip, city of residence, state/prov of residence, country of residence, citizenship country; correspondence name/address/telephone/fax/email or Customer Number; application information such as title lines, suggested classification, tech center, total drawing sheets, docket number, application type; representative registration numbers; domestic priority information; foreign priority information; assignee information; plant genus/species where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ADS should include repeated blocks for additional inventors and other repeated items where needed. Representative information must list ten or fewer representatives or be indicated by reference to a Customer Number (see 37 CFR 1.32). The correspondence information may be indicated by reference to a Customer Number. Use of ADS is encouraged to aid accurate capture of inventor names/citizenship/residence and other metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office reliance on application data sheet over oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will rely upon information supplied in the application data sheet over an oath or declaration to capture the data even where the type of information supplied (citizenship, inventorship) is governed by the oath or declaration according to statute or other rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the oath or declaration contains the correct information and the ADS does not, the ADS must be corrected by submission of a request for correction and a supplemental ADS. Even when ADS is used, certain corrections (see citizenship correction rules) may require supplemental oaths/declarations. Applicants are encouraged to file ADS or supplemental ADS to ensure the issued patent reflects correct data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventor citizenship mismatches
rubrics_metrics.description: If citizenship is incorrectly set forth in an oath/declaration, the inventor must submit a supplemental oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 with the correct citizenship; a supplemental application data sheet cannot be used to correct the citizenship error in the oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the ADS correctly sets forth an inventor's citizenship but the executed 37 CFR 1.63 declaration sets forth a different incorrect citizenship, the Office will capture the citizenship from the ADS, BUT applicant must still submit a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 by the inventor setting forth the correct citizenship. If the error is one of residence, no change would be required (37 CFR 1.76(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of typographical/transliteration errors in inventor names
rubrics_metrics.description: A typographical or transliteration error in the spelling of an inventor's name requires only notification of the error to the Office; a supplemental application data sheet to correct the spelling is strongly encouraged but a supplemental oath or declaration is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant merely files a statement notifying the Office of the typographical/transliteration error without submitting an ADS or supplemental ADS, any patent to issue is less likely to reflect the correct spelling because the spelling is taken from the oath or declaration or any subsequently filed ADS. The Office strongly encourages filing an ADS or supplemental ADS to correct spelling errors (see MPEP § 605.04(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution and identity requirements for oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration filed as part of a nonprovisional application must: (1) be executed (signed) in accordance with either 37 CFR 1.66 or 1.68; (2) identify each inventor by full name, including the family name, and at least one given name without abbreviation together with any other given name or initial; (3) identify the country of citizenship of each inventor; and (4) state that the person making the oath or declaration believes the named inventor(s) to be the original and first inventor(s) of the subject matter which is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no minimum age to sign, but the signer must be competent to sign (understand the document). See MPEP §§ 602.01–602.05 for additional execution and venue guidance (seals, venue, use of declarations vs oaths).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive statements required in oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to paragraph (a) requirements, the oath/declaration must: (1) identify the application to which it is directed; (2) state that the person making the oath/declaration has reviewed and understands the contents of the application, including the claims, as amended by any amendment specifically referred to in the oath/declaration; and (3) state that the person acknowledges the duty to disclose to the Office all information known to be material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oath/declaration functions as an affirmation that the inventor has reviewed and understands the application and acknowledges disclosure duties; failure to include these statements can make the oath/declaration defective and trigger requirements for supplemental filings or notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses and foreign priority information in oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless such information is supplied on an ADS in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76, the oath/declaration must also identify: (1) the mailing address, and the residence if different, of each inventor; and (2) any foreign application for patent (or inventor's certificate) for which a claim for priority is made pursuant to 37 CFR 1.55, and any foreign application having a filing date before that of the application on which priority is claimed, by specifying the application number, country, day, month, and year of its filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all foreign applications were filed within 12 months of the U.S. filing date, applicant is required only to recite the first such foreign application of which priority is claimed. If the information is omitted, form paragraphs (e.g., 6.05, 6.05.08) may be used to notify applicant that the oath/declaration is defective for omission of foreign application identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: When new oath/declaration is not required for continuation or divisional (37 CFR 1.63(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration is not required in a continuation or divisional application provided that: (i) the prior nonprovisional application contained an oath/declaration as prescribed by 37 CFR 1.63(a)-(c); (ii) the continuation/divisional was filed by all or by fewer than all of the inventors named in the prior application; (iii) the specification and drawings filed in the continuation/divisional contain no matter that would have been new matter in the prior application; and (iv) a copy of the executed oath/declaration filed in the prior application, showing the signature or an indication thereon that it was signed, is submitted for the continuation/divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy submitted must be accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the names of persons who are not inventors in the continuation/divisional if fewer inventors are named. Additional documentary requirements apply when the prior application had 1.47 status or inventor(s) later joined in the prior application (see 1.63(d)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a new oath/declaration is required (continuation-in-part and new inventors)
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration must be filed in any continuation-in-part application, and must be filed in a continuation or divisional application naming an inventor not named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation-in-part may name all, more, or fewer inventors than the prior application, but a new oath is required to reflect the changed inventor set or new matter. If the continuation/divisional copies a prior oath, include required statements per 1.63(d)(2)-(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration in lieu of oath (37 CFR 1.68) / statutory declaration (28 U.S.C. 1746)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document required to be under oath may be subscribed to by a written declaration (37 CFR 1.68) if the declarant is warned that willful false statements are punishable (18 U.S.C. 1001); the declarant must set forth that statements of own knowledge are true and statements on information and belief are believed to be true. The USPTO will accept a statutory declaration under 28 U.S.C. 1746 in lieu of an oath or 37 CFR 1.68 declaration, if it otherwise complies with legal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 37 CFR 1.68 declaration need not be ribboned to other papers even if signed abroad. When using 28 U.S.C. 1746, use the appropriate execution clause depending on whether executed within the U.S. or outside (e.g., 'under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America' vs 'under penalty of perjury').

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments and new matter; supplemental oath/declaration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a preliminary amendment is present on the filing date and the oath/declaration does not refer to the preliminary amendment, applicant must ensure the preliminary amendment does not contain new matter; if it does, applicant must provide a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 referring to the preliminary amendment. Failure to submit such a supplemental oath/declaration removes safeguards implied in the oath/declaration requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can avoid needing an oath referring to a preliminary amendment by incorporating amendments into the specification (including a new set of claims) when filing. Applicants are strongly encouraged to avoid submitting preliminary amendments to minimize Office burden and avoid delays. During examination, an examiner may require a supplemental oath/declaration, an amendment that cancels the unsupported subject matter, or a request for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the application/specification in an oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.63 requires the oath or declaration to identify the specification to which it is directed. While the Office's suggested form includes application number, filing date, etc., it is not essential that all spaces be completed. Minimum acceptable combinations supplied on filing date include: (A) name of inventor(s) and reference to an attached specification attached at execution and submitted on filing; (B) name of inventor(s) and attorney docket number which was on the specification as filed; or (C) name of inventor(s) and title of the invention which was on the specification as filed. For oaths/declarations filed after the filing date, acceptable minima include combinations such as serial number and filing date; attorney docket number on specification; title of the invention and attached specification; title and cover letter accurately identifying the application (application number or serial number and filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any specification filed attached to an oath/declaration on a date later than the application filing date will not be compared with the specification submitted on filing. Absent contrary statements, the attached specification will be presumed a copy of the specification and amendments filed in the USPTO to obtain the filing date. Use appropriate identification or risk the oath/declaration being considered defective (see form paragraph 6.05 and 6.05.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner form paragraphs for defective oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides form paragraphs to notify applicants when an oath or declaration is defective (¶ 6.05 Oath or Declaration Defective) and specific form paragraphs for common defects (e.g., ¶ 6.05.01 Improper Execution; ¶ 6.05.08 Identification of Foreign Applications Omitted; ¶ 6.05.20 Specification Not Identified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.05 must precede the specific defect paragraph. Examiner notes indicate which paragraphs must accompany 6.05. If none of the form paragraphs apply, an appropriate explanation of the defect should immediately follow the 6.05 paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of original oaths/declarations encouraged and retention of originals
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy (photocopy or facsimile) of an originally executed oath or declaration is encouraged to be filed, especially since applications are maintained in electronic form; the original should be retained by applicant or representative as evidence of authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authenticity is questioned, the USPTO may require submission of the original. See 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1)(ii). Declarations are preferred over oaths because seals on oaths cannot be adequately scanned for retention in the Image File Wrapper; many states' oaths need not be impressed with a seal, but the Office strongly encourages declarations for scannability and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and criminality warning (18 U.S.C. 1001)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 18 U.S.C. 1001, whoever knowingly and willfully falsifies, conceals, or covers up a material fact, or makes any false/fictitious/fraudulent statements or uses any false writing knowing it to contain false statements, shall be fined up to $10,000 or imprisoned up to five years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oaths/declarations and statutory declarations must include the required warning language about willful false statements. Use of the statutory declaration clause or 37 CFR 1.68's clause is necessary to render declarations acceptable and to put declarants on notice of penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and treatment of new claims not originally claimed (supplemental oath requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim is presented for matter not originally claimed or embraced in the original statement of invention in the specification, a supplemental oath or declaration is required (37 CFR 1.67; see MPEP § 603).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new claim matter is presented, applicant must submit supplemental oath/declaration referencing the new matter. For applications filed prior to certain rule changes, a surcharge may be required when supplemental oath references preliminary amendments (see MPEP discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for declarations in U.S. national stage (35 U.S.C. 371) and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations filed in a U.S. national stage application under 35 U.S.C. 371 have identification requirements described elsewhere (see MPEP § 1896). Supplemental oaths/declarations will be required in applications where oaths/declarations are not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 but contain sufficient information to identify the specifications to which they apply as detailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any variance from guidelines for identification will only be considered upon filing of a petition for waiver of the rules under 37 CFR 1.183 accompanied by a petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(f)).
